prompt: Your company is transitioning from traditional password management to PAM-based authentication. In a review session, a colleague suggests storing encrypted user passwords in `/etc/passwd`. What do you make of this suggestion?
choices: This is a good practice as `/etc/passwd` is the standard password store
This is not a recommended practice; encrypted passwords should be stored in `/etc/shadow` instead
Encrypted passwords should be stored in `/etc/pam.conf` instead
Passwords should be stored only in the LDAP directory, never on the local system
explanation: This is not a recommended practice; encrypted passwords should be stored in `/etc/shadow` instead, which is readable only by privileged accounts.
